editorial:
Ever feel like family gatherings are just one big disaster waiting to happen? You will totally relate to Wabisuke in this story. When his father-in-law passes away, he has to deal with a three-day funeral in the family home. Instead of just being a sad time, it turns into a wild ride of social rules, awkward moments, and family secrets. You get to see how the characters try to look perfect on the outside while everything is falling apart behind the scenes. It feels like a peek into a world where following the rules is more important than actually being sad.

What really makes this work is how funny it is without trying too hard. The acting is great, and the way the scenes jump from quiet moments to total chaos keeps you interested. One downside is that some of the cultural customs might feel a bit slow at first, but you will get the hang of it quickly. If you love movies that poke fun at tradition, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection if you want the best picture quality possible.
endingExplained: As the funeral wraps up, you see that the family didn't really change, but they found a way to survive the chaos together. The movie ends with the family finally finishing the long list of rituals. The big takeaway is that the funeral was more about the living people showing off their status than it was about the dead man. It wraps up on a light note, showing that life just keeps moving forward despite the stress.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family comedies and quirky human behavior.
